result:
A logged model's status message now survives conversion to its serialized (protobuf) form and back, so a failed model keeps "Upload failed".

**Cause:** `LoggedModel.from_proto` already read `status_message`, but `LoggedModel.to_proto` in `mlflow/entities/logged_model.py` never wrote it. Any model that went through the serialized form came back with an empty status message.

**Fix:** I added one line to `to_proto` so it sets `status_message=self.status_message` along with the other descriptive fields. Nothing else changed.

**Test:** I added `tests/entities/test_logged_model.py`, since there was no entity test file for logged models yet. It creates a failed model with "Upload failed", checks that the serialized form contains the message, and checks that reading it back gives the same status and message. It passes. I only ran this new test, not the wider suite.

+from mlflow.entities.logged_model import LoggedModel
+from mlflow.entities.logged_model_status import LoggedModelStatus
+
+
+def test_logged_model_proto_round_trip_preserves_status_message():
+    model = LoggedModel(
+        experiment_id="1",
+        model_id="m-123",
+        name="model",
+        artifact_location="file:///tmp/artifacts",
+        creation_timestamp=1,
+        last_updated_timestamp=2,
+        status=LoggedModelStatus.FAILED,
+        status_message="Upload failed",
+    )
+    proto = model.to_proto()
+    assert proto.info.status_message == "Upload failed"
+
+    restored = LoggedModel.from_proto(proto)
+    assert restored.status == LoggedModelStatus.FAILED
+    assert restored.status_message == "Upload failed"
